mods.name: Fuel On Demand
mods.summary: Forges, campfires and chem stations burn fuel only while they are actually working. No overburn on the last item, the fire goes out when the craft queue empties, and a jammed station goes dark until you make room. Leftover fuel is kept. Empty stations still burn for heat. Server-side only; players install nothing.

mods.name: Stash n' Fetch
mods.summary: Stash, fetch and craft from storage — without ever opening a box. One key sends your whole haul into the containers around you. Another pulls back exactly what you're short of. The crafting window counts those containers as your backpack, and an Add to list button turns any recipe into a shopping list it keeps score of.

mods.name: POI Map
mods.summary: The vanilla map shows terrain and your own way points — not one point of interest. This puts them all on it: tier-colored, named on hover, listed by distance in a searchable panel. Then it tells you what is inside each one — books, cars, guns, crops, safes — and how many sleepers are waiting. Plus the preview render the game never shows.

mods.name: Drone Automation Kit
mods.summary: Server-side 7 Days to Die mod: junk-drone modules that automate chores while the drone follows you. Auto-Loot, Auto-Salvage, Auto-Harvest, Auto-Repair and Auto-Plant all work as if you did it yourself; Auto-Defense makes the drone a bodyguard; Overclock and Wide-Band Antenna boost the rest. Craftable, quality-scaled.

mods.name: Mega Trees (25x)
mods.tagline: One Seed and the Wood of 25
mods.summary: Server-side mod (Game V3.0+) for 25x mega trees: combine 25 saplings into one giant that harvests like 25 trees. Eight species including a coal-bearing burnt pine. Saves space, cuts tree count.

mods.name: ScoutMap
mods.summary: A HUD minimap that names what you are looking at. Every point of interest is drawn and coloured by tier, and the building you are standing in is named under the map. Hostiles appear only once they are awake and already hunting you. Runs entirely on your own client, including on dedicated servers that have never heard of it.

mods.name: Loot Magnet
mods.summary: A placeable block that loots nearby bags, containers and dropped items as if you opened them yourself — loot stage, Lucky Looter and loot buffs all apply. Chain storage chests onto it and the haul spreads across them, topping off matching stacks first. Upgrade it in place through three tiers for more reach and speed. Server-side only.

mods.name: Control Panel
mods.tagline: Every Mod's Settings and Hotkeys in One Screen
mods.summary: One settings screen for every mod you have, and one place that finally tells you which of them are fighting over the same key. Tune any mod from inside the game — mine or anyone else's — and see every hotkey on your install in one table, with the collisions called out and the free keys listed.

mods.name: Auto Nailgun
mods.tagline: Hold It and Your Base Repairs and Upgrades Itself
mods.summary: Hold your nailgun in your own land claim: every damaged block around you is repaired and every block that can climb a tier does - frames to wood to cobble to concrete to steel - at vanilla cost, XP and swing speed. It stops where your materials do, and stands down on blood moon. Client-side; servers install nothing.

mods.name: Accessory Slots
mods.summary: Extra equipment slots on a new Accessories tab: a necklace, a bracelet and two rings by default, and other mods add their own - like Glider's glider slot. Worn items give their bonuses like armor and follow your world's armor rules on death. A framework: install it for a mod that uses it. Server and every client, EAC off.

mods.name: Zipline
mods.summary: Ride a steel cable between rooftops, up to 512 blocks a span. Slide down on gravity, haul back up hand over hand, or wire in a generator for a motor both ways. New worlds hide a few old ziplines on forest-town rooftops to find. Riders count as in a vehicle on horde night. Idea by Liz (More2Me 4Life). Server + every client, EAC off.

mods.name: Glider
mods.tagline: Jump Off Anything and Float Down
mods.summary: Deployable gliders: jump, then jump again in mid-air to open a wing and float down from any roof, cliff or tower. Five gliders from a scrap parachute to the gas-thrust Thruster Wings, five glider mods with quality, vehicle-style steering. Requires Accessory Slots. Server and every client, EAC off.

mods.name: SteadyFrame
mods.summary: Makes horde night cheaper, not smaller. A server-side mod that attacks the real per-tick cost of a blood moon — the AI think budget, the block-stability solver, pathfinding — plus a CPU-aware governor that tunes itself to your hardware. The same horde costs the server less, so it stacks on difficulty mods that raise them. Clients install nothin

mods.name: Turret Resupply
mods.tagline: Turrets Reload From Your Ammo Boxes
mods.summary: Turrets reload themselves from your storage boxes. Keep ammo in a box near your turrets and traps and they stay loaded - with the ammo you chose (AP stays AP), or the best in the box if you never chose. A turret that ran dry is re-armed. Never a box a player has open. Server-side only: players install nothing.

mods.name: Quest Biome Indicator
mods.tagline: See the Biome Before You Take the Job
mods.summary: A trader's job list gives you the tier, the distance and the building — never the biome, which is what really decides how the run goes. Quest Biome adds it to every offered quest, colour-coded, before you accept. Buried supplies included. Works even on servers that don't run it. Client-side, EAC off.

mods.name: Materialist
mods.summary: Ask the game where anything comes from: /mat where duct tape ranks every source in the game with real drop odds, read from your own loot tables. Then it finds it for you — containers, ground, ore veins, trees, nests, even live chickens light up through walls. Client-side, works on vanilla dedicated servers. Requires EAC off.

mods.name: Mindless Zombies
mods.summary: EXPERIMENTAL. Vanilla zombies path to your weakest block and pick your base apart. Mindless flattens that: block hardness stops mattering, so they come straight at you and through whatever's in the way. Slower by day, a surge on a blood moon, they enrage when shot and gunfire brings screamers. Server-side — clients install nothing, EAC stays on.

mods.name: SteadyView
mods.tagline: Adaptive Graphics That See the Fight Coming
mods.summary: Keeps your frame rate up in a fight without making the game look worse the rest of the time. Tier 0 is your own settings, so with headroom it does nothing at all. It watches frame time and how many zombies are near you, so it steps down as the crowd arrives, not after your frames collapse. Client-side, and it never writes your saved settings.

mods.name: Sandbox Settings Randomizer
mods.tagline: Roll a New World Every Time
mods.summary: Re-roll your game settings on a schedule, streamer-style. Adds a Randomize button and padlocks to the Sandbox Options screen, plus an auto-randomizer that fires manually, every morning, or after each blood moon. Seeded, reproducible, per-save. Install on the server; players can add it too so rolls land without a rejoin. Requires EAC off.

mods.name: Sound Radar
mods.summary: Play with the sound off and still know what is happening. Arrows at the edge of your screen point at the hostiles you cannot see - direction, real name, and how dangerous it is. Nothing is drawn over the fight: a filled dot is a body still alive, a hollow ring is a noise, and a wall being chewed gets a warning. Client-side; servers install nothing.

mods.name: ProjectZ MasteryMark
mods.tagline: Know Which Books You Can Scrap
mods.summary: A read perk book is spare the moment you read it. A skill magazine is not — in Project Z, 8 of them craft the mastery magazine above it. This marks the difference: the game's own scrap icon on books with nothing left to give, the count still owed on the ones worth keeping, and a blue mark for a line whose mastery finished without it.

mods.name: Queue Priority
mods.summary: Vanilla gives you one gesture on a queued craft: cancel it and take the ingredients back. Alt + click a queue slot to craft it next, Alt + right-click to send it to the back - and Alt + right-click the job in progress to split it, so the one in the pan finishes and the rest waits its turn. Client-side; works on servers that don't have it.

mods.name: Vanilla Fixes
mods.summary: Four bugs in the base game, one mod. A quest from an item that never gets a location, or whose Stay Within never turns green. A treasure map read below y=10 that never places its chest. A modded forge showing a smelting panel the game already switched off.

mods.name: ProjectZ-WalkerSims Boss Fix
mods.summary: Running WalkerSim2 on a ProjectZ server? Snow, desert and burnt forest turn into boss conveyor belts at night — 65-72% of the biome spawn pool becomes 30,000-240,000 HP bosses. WalkerSim disables the vanilla biome spawner, removing the maxcount cap that kept them rare. This puts that rarity back. Server-side XML, no DLL.

mods.name: Fuel Top-Off
mods.tagline: One Key Fuels the Whole Queue
mods.summary: Queue half an hour of crafting on five minutes of wood and vanilla lets the fire go out. Press one key inside a forge, campfire or chemistry station and exactly enough wood or coal goes in from your backpack to see the whole queue through - and it lights the station if it had gone out. Client-side; servers install nothing.

mods.name: Chat Events
mods.tagline: Let Your Chat Drop Hordes Bosses and Debuffs on You
mods.summary: Hand your chat the controls. Console-callable buffs any bot fires with buffplayer: trip them, burn them, blur their screen, or drop a gamestage-scaled horde or a boss on their head. Server-side only, no dependencies. Project Z, if installed, adds 60 more meter buffs. A redeem never spawns nothing - buy too high and it downgrades and multiplies.

mods.name: Player Beacon
mods.tagline: Let Your Bot See Vehicles Claims and Traders
mods.summary: Your bot can read a player's position and health, and nothing else that matters. Player Beacon publishes what a server console cannot see - is this player on a vehicle, in a land claim, or inside a trader area - as plain CVars you read with "cvar get". Server-side, XML only, read-only. Clients install nothing.

mods.name: Hidden Passcodes
mods.summary: 7 Days to Die draws your storage passcode in plain text while you type it, so it is readable on stream, in a recording, on a shared screen or over a shoulder. This masks it to dots and adds the game's own reveal button. Server-side and XML-only: clients install nothing and EAC stays on.
